sources.citation: Kaba, Elizabeth. 1988. Esquisse phonologique du mmaala (dialecte yambassa). Mémoire de maîtrise, Université de Yaoundé, Faculté des Lettres et Sciences Humaines (dir. Rose Zoé Obianga). 80 pp. (88-page scan, MPI Language Description Heritage, hdl:11858/00-001M-0000-0012-7FB9-9)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing about word stress. Ch. 2 'Unités suprasegmentales: les tonèmes' (p. 38) gives three tonemes (haut, bas, bas-haut); Part 3 'Prosodie' (pp. 70-75) defines prosody as pitch, intensity and duration but then treats only sentence intonation (declarative falling curve, interrogative rise, tone lowering). The word 'accent' occurs once, in the idiom 'mettre l'accent sur l'intonation' (p. 71). Space-tolerant search of the whole scanned text for accent/intensité/durée/proéminence found no other hit. The earlier scan's not reachable by automated download was the pure.mpg.de bot wall; the REST end…

sources.citation: Boyd, Virginia Lee. 2015. The phonological systems of the Mbam languages of Cameroon with a focus on vowels and vowel harmony. PhD dissertation, Universiteit Leiden. LOT Dissertation Series 410. 413 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §2.7 'Mmala phonological overview' (pp. 135-159); §2.7.5 Tone (pp. 158-159): 'Mmala has a two-tone system underlyingly, high and low'; noun melodies L, H, LH, HL; verb melodies L, HL, H with H spread. The only occurrence of 'stress' in the whole thesis is inside a quoted Dixon & Aikhenvald (2002) definition of the phonological word (p. 257); no stress statement for Mmala or any Mbam language. §1.6.5.3 (p. 21) lists the Mmala literature: Paulian 1986b, Idiata 2000, Kaba 1988, surveys.
